subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Diodes: One-Way Valves for Current
description: One-minute skill: Diodes: One-Way Valves for Current.

hook.text: A diode lets current flow in one direction and blocks it in the other. Simple, powerful.

buildup.text: Forward bias shrinks the depletion zone. Reverse bias widens it — no current gets through.

discovery.text: Silicon diodes need about 0.7 V forward bias to turn on. Below that, they stay off.

twist.text: Push too much reverse voltage and the diode breaks down — current surges through.

climax.text: Rectifiers in every phone charger use diodes to convert AC wall power into DC.

punchline.text: Current flows one way through a diode — the simplest semiconductor trick.

quiz.question: What voltage is needed to forward-bias a silicon diode?
